name: TCG 2010 (Edison era, Master Rule 1 baseline)
description: The DUEL_MODE_MR1 composite plus two additional flags researched and confirmed against period (2008-2011) Konami rulebooks and engine tests for TCG play at SJC Edison (2010-04-24): DUEL_TCG_FAST_EFFECT_IGNITION (the broader pre-2012 TCG ignition-priority condition) and DUEL_0_ATK_DESTROYED (0-ATK monsters still destroyed each other on a tie before the May-2011 rulebook added an exception). See docs/research/edison-rules.md for the full evidence table; several other candidate flags remain unresolved (known_gaps) rather than guessed. Synchro Monsters are legal; Xyz/Pendulum/Link do not exist yet.

era.official_ruleset_label: Konami 'OFFICIAL RULEBOOK' Version 7.1 (current as of 2010-03-30, 25 days before SJC Edison; EDOPro calls the underlying preset 'Master Rule 1')

differences_from_modern.summary: The turn player may activate ignition effects with priority after a summon or chain end (OCG-style condition, part of the MR1 baseline).
The turn-1 player draws in their first Draw Phase.
Only one Field Spell can be face-up at a time.
A negated Special Summon still counts against 'only once per turn/duel' summon restrictions.

Ignition Effects can be activated at any point the chain is empty during the turn player's Main Phase, from any location - not just as an immediate response to a Summon/chain-end event (broader TCG-style priority, in force until the TCG adopted the narrower OCG-style condition on 2012-04-25, two years after Edison). Confirmed against the Konami Official Rulebook (V7.0 Dec-2008 through V8.0 Nov-2011, wording unchanged across that whole span) and by an engine test that fails without this flag.

When two monsters with equal, non-zero-excepted ATK (including 0 ATK vs. 0 ATK) destroy each other in battle, both are destroyed - the 0-ATK exception ('neither is destroyed') was not added to the rulebook until the May-2011 'New Master Rules' edition, 13 months after Edison. Confirmed by an engine test that fails without this flag.

known_gaps.summary: Simultaneous Trigger Effect ordering (SEGOC): the period-primary Official Rulebook (2008-2011, bracketing Edison) describes a simple two-tier system (turn player's triggers first, freely ordered; then the opponent's) with no mandatory-before-optional split and no 'earlier trigger first' tiebreak - contradicting EdisonFormat.com's own claimed four-tier structure, which is only traceable to a 2012 forum thread whose participants assert (without period documentation) that it was already tournament-floor practice. Neither of the two specific mechanics DUEL_TCG_SEGOC_NONPUBLIC/DUEL_TCG_SEGOC_FIRSTTRIGGER implement (hidden-zone trigger folding; first-event-only restriction among several simultaneous events) is addressed by any period source found in either direction. Left unresolved rather than guessed; see docs/research/edison-rules.md row 9 for the full evidence and a candidate research lead (an unlocated later rulebook edition between Nov-2011 and 2017).

Three further candidate flags (DUEL_USE_TRAPS_IN_NEW_CHAIN, DUEL_TRIGGER_WHEN_PRIVATE_KNOWLEDGE, DUEL_CAN_REPOS_IF_NON_SUMPLAYER) were researched but no period source (primary or otherwise reliable) was found addressing the specific behaviour in either direction - each rests only on an uncorroborated modern community claim or a card-specific ruling that doesn't clearly generalize. Left out of the flag set rather than added on unresolved evidence; see docs/research/edison-rules.md rows 2, 4, 8.
Extra Deck size limit for 2010 (15) is entered here from the EDOPro MR1 preset defaults, not yet from a period rulebook citation.

notes: Named -edison to leave room for splitting the long 'MR1' span into finer sourced eras later. As of the roadmap-item-5 research pass (docs/research/edison-rules.md), this is no longer a pure DUEL_MODE_MR1 profile: DUEL_TCG_FAST_EFFECT_IGNITION and DUEL_0_ATK_DESTROYED were added on period-rulebook evidence and confirmed with failing/passing engine tests (tests/engine/test_historical_behaviour.py). Several other candidate flags remain deliberately unresolved (known_gaps) rather than enabled on name-plausibility or uncorroborated community claims alone; this profile should stay 'partial' in format.json's implementation_status until those are settled.
